newsitem.title: DUBAI: Rushdie death edict cannot be changed - Iran MP.
newsitem.headline: Rushdie death edict cannot be changed - Iran MP.

text.p: An Iranian parliamentarian has said the death edict, or fatwa, against British author Salman Rushdie for alleged blasphemy cannot be changed.

The deputy chairman of parliament's foreign affairs committee, Mahmoud Do'a'i, said on Friday "the death sentence on Rushdie, the apostate, was an unchangeable religious decree" accepted by all Moslem Sunni and Shi'ite scholars, Iran television reported.

He made the remarks in response to a call by former French culture minister Jack Lang for Europe to step up pressure on Tehran to drop the edict, said the television, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC).

Earlier this week, Indian-born Rushdie addressed the French parliament's foreign affairs committee which is chaired by Lang. The author urged Europeans to stand up to Iran and defend their traditional values, such as freedom of speech.
The late Iranian spiritual leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini issued the death edict against Rushdie in 1989 for what some Moslems regard as blasphemy in his book "The Satanic Verses".
